skill.name: git-workflow-enforcer
skill.description: Guides consistent Git workflows for commit messages, branch names, pull request templates, Git hooks, protected branches, and changelogs.
skill.summary: Enforces practical Git workflow conventions for commits, branches, pull requests, hooks, and changelogs.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are Markdown formatting false positives. The confirmed risks are local Git hook templates and a global Git configuration command that points to ~/.gitmessage. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Global Git configuration changes user-level behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer repository-local configuration or ask for explicit confirmation before using git config --global with a home-directory template.

remediation.issue: Git hook templates can execute commands during future commits.
remediation.suggestion: Present hook contents for review and require explicit approval before writing or enabling hooks.

remediation.issue: Shell examples include npm and npx command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Do not run package commands automatically. Explain local dependency execution and request approval first.

remediation.issue: The example secret check is only keyword matching.
remediation.suggestion: Document it as a basic guard and recommend a dedicated secret scanning tool for real enforcement.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time to unclear commits, inconsistent branch names, and incomplete pull requests. This skill provides repeatable Git workflow guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Checks for existing workflow conventions in repository templates and contribution files.
Suggests Conventional Commits subjects, bodies, scopes, and issue references.
Provides branch naming patterns with validation criteria.
Drafts pull request templates and commit message template content.
Offers sample Git hook templates for commit and pre-commit validation.
Gives changelog generation guidance from Conventional Commits history.
limitations: It does not enforce remote branch protection settings by itself.
Hook examples require review before local installation.
The secret check example uses simple keyword matching only.
Changelog quality depends on the existing commit history.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Commits
use_cases.description: Define commit message, branch, and pull request conventions before a shared release cycle.

use_cases.title: Prepare Repository Templates
use_cases.description: Draft a pull request template, commit message template, and hook guidance for a new project.

use_cases.title: Review Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Check recent commits and branch names before generating release notes or opening a merge request.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Conventional Commits message for these changes: [describe the change]. Include a short subject and optional body.

prompt_templates.title: Name a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a branch name for this task: [task summary]. Use the project convention if one exists.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Pull Request Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request template for this repository. Include description, change type, testing, checklist, and related issues.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Git Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository workflow for commit, branch, hook, PR, and changelog practices. Identify gaps and propose safe improvements.

output_examples.input: Prepare a commit for fixing a failed login state.
output_examples.output: A Conventional Commit subject for authentication, plus body notes for user impact, validation steps, and the related ticket.

output_examples.input: Create a pull request checklist for an API change.
output_examples.output: A pull request template with description, change type, testing notes, reviewer checklist, warning checks, and related issue fields.

output_examples.input: Review recent commits before a release.
output_examples.output: A short workflow report covering commit format drift, missing issue references, release note readiness, and suggested cleanup steps.

best_practices: Review existing repository conventions before proposing new rules.
Ask before creating hooks or changing Git configuration.
Keep commit subjects short, imperative, and tied to one logical change.
anti_patterns: Do not rewrite team conventions without maintainer approval.
Do not install Git hooks that run commands without review.
Do not treat simple keyword checks as complete secret scanning.

faq.question: Does this skill make commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides commit messages and workflow files. The user or agent must still choose when to commit.

faq.question: Can it enforce branch protections on GitHub?
faq.answer: It can recommend branch protection settings. It does not change remote repository settings by itself.

faq.question: Does it support Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Conventional Commits types, optional scopes, short subjects, bodies, and issue references.

faq.question: Can it create pull request templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a standard pull request template structure with testing and review checklist sections.

faq.question: Are the Git hook examples safe to install?
faq.answer: They should be reviewed first. Hooks can run local commands during commits and may affect developer workflows.

faq.question: Does it detect leaked secrets?
faq.answer: It includes a simple keyword check example. Use a dedicated secret scanner for reliable detection.
